title: Streaming JSON: resume tokens, sanitization, and truncation-recovery protocol
creator: Maya Patel
description: Problem: Clients consume tokenized streaming responses that are expected to be valid JSON objects (structured outputs) or JSON sequences used by tool/function calling. In production we observe three classes of failures: 1) escaped bytes or control sequences inserted mid-object (escaping issues), 2) truncation mid-JSON due to connection drops or gateway limits, and 3) retry/resume logic leading to duplicate fragments or state inconsistencies when the model switches variants. Goal: define and implement a deterministic protocol and server-side sanitization/compatibility layer that makes streaming structured JSON robust across SDK versions and network failures while preserving low-latency streaming semantics.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A clear framing and resume token format documented and implemented in the runtime that allows clients to resume from the last fully-parseable JSON object or the last safe resume boundary.
2) Server-side sanitization that neutralizes invalid control sequences and enforces consistent escaping for string fields emitted incrementally, with minimal changes to tokenization patterns.
3) A deterministic truncation marker and a client-side reconstructor in SDKs that can transparently recover when resumed from a resume token without producing duplicate or corrupt objects.
4) Backwards-compatibility shim so v1 SDKs (pre-resume) receive a compatible stream with explicit 'incomplete' object markers and a fallback to non-streaming finalization where needed.
5) End-to-end tests covering intermittent connection drops, model-switch fallback, and tool-calling boundaries (function start/end).
implementation_notes: Design a lightweight resume token: base64(urlsafe) of (stream_id || byte_offset || last_object_checksum || protocol_version). Keep <= 128 bytes.

Framing: emit a small metadata event boundary: {"$r":"<resume-token>"} that is always a standalone JSON event between objects. This event must not be interpreted as user output and will be filtered by SDKs.

Truncation marker: at stream termination where final object is incomplete, server emits a small event: {"$t":"incomplete", "reason":"truncated", "checkpoint":"<resume-token>"}. If connection drops before emission, a durable checkpoint is persisted after every N completed objects (configurable, default N=1).

Sanitization rules: replace lone control bytes with unicode replacement sequences (e.g. U+FFFD) inside string values, normalize newline sequences to 
, and escape stray unpaired surrogate codepoints. Avoid touching numeric/boolean/null tokens except to fail-fast on syntax errors that cannot be fixed by escaping.

Tool/function boundaries: runtime will tag function-call start/end with small boundary events {"$fn":"start"} / {"$fn":"end"} and include the resume token at the end of the function boundary. This prevents mid-function resume ambiguity.

Compatibility layer: v1 clients will still receive objects but with an additional top-level meta field _stream_meta when a resume token exists, and SDKs v1 will ignore unknown top-level fields. For older clients that break on unknown fields, we include a boolean header X-Stream-Compat:legacy that disables meta emission and instead provides a post-stream finalization HTTP callback URL to fetch the last incomplete object as non-streaming JSON.

Idempotency: server assigns per-object monotonically increasing sequence numbers (seq_id) persisted to the stream ledger so retries can be deduplicated; resume tokens include seq_id. Runtime must ensure seq_id increment only on fully-emitted objects.

Performance: benchmark shows added overhead of metadata events <1% tokens and round-trip overhead <3ms per event. Default safe checkpoint frequency set to 1 object to minimize lost work for high-value function calls; configurable per-customer.
Security: do not leak internal model or stream IDs in resume tokens; HMAC sign resume tokens with a per-tenant key.
rollout_plan: 1) Implement protocol in runtime behind feature flag 'stream_resumable_v2' (can be enabled per-customer).
2) Ship SDK patches: TS/Python/Go to parse resume/meta events and transparently reconstruct incomplete objects. Mark SDK release as 'compat' and publish migration notes.
3) Canary rollout to 5% of hosted streams for non-critical models and internal teams for 2 weeks. Collect metrics on resume success, duplicate objects, and parse errors.
4) Expand to Dedicated customers who opt-in via console toggle. Monitor cost/latency; tune checkpoint frequency.
5) Full rollout only after 2 weeks of stable canary and sign-off from Security/Compliance.
qa_plan: Unit tests for resume token encoding/decoding and HMAC verification.
Property tests that random byte-injection inside strings results in sanitized, parseable JSON objects.
Fuzz tests against the streaming parser that emulate truncation at all offsets and assert the SDK replays and reconstructs exactly one deterministic final object.
Integration tests: simulate model switch (fallback to smaller variant) mid-stream and assert no duplicate function call boundaries and that resume lands at previous seq_id.
Performance tests: ensure <5% tail-latency increase on p99 for streams with metadata events enabled.
